NorthGlen nearing contract renewal; primary asks: add EU region capacity, lower tail latency for checkout flows, contractual burst capacity for Black Friday-like events, and standard security attestations for on-prem/VPC options. Redwood proposed 12-month extension with committed base + burst pool; SE to run EU latency bench and provide SOC/ISO artifacts. transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey all, thanks for joining — I'll kick us off. We're on for about an hour; main agenda is renewal and the EU uplift.
[00:12] Amira: Hello, yes thanks. We got the renewal notice, and the team wanted to use this call to align on numbers and on the latency targets for checkout.
[00:20] Carlos: Quick intro - I'm Carlos, Redwood SE, I own performance/ops for the EU stack.
[00:27] Jonas: Jonas here - infrastructure. We'll want to understand peering/VPC requirements and the private option if we need it.
[00:33] Sofia: Hi, Sofia from procurement - I'll be tracking contract language and timeline.
[00:38] Maya: Great. Amira, could you restate your high-level success criteria so we're synced?
[00:44] Amira: Sure. One, maintain sub-200ms 95thpct for token-gen inside EU for checkout flows. Two, dedicated burst pool we can call for sale days up to 3x baseline. Three, data residency — logs retained in region and plus SOC2 artifacts for our auditors. Four, minimal change to our engineering integration.
[01:05] Maya: Perfect. On the 95th percentile latency, that's a tight target but doable with dedicated nodes in EU-west + KV caching. Carlos will talk specifics.
[01:15] Carlos: Yeah, quick note — the runtime supports continuous batching and prefix cache; however checkout flows are short but very latency sensitive so we'll likely recommend smaller batch sizes and aggressive cache warm-up. Also a note — our auto-routing can failover to US if capacity starves, but that will break residency so we can set policy to avoid cross-region fallback.
[01:40] Jonas: So how do we isolate that? We need a hard fail-over policy not to cross borders. Also how about network egress costs?
[01:49] Carlos: We can set routing policy scoped to region and to plan tier. If we do a dedicated EU pool for NorthGlen, failover would only happen within EU variants. Egress is only if you cross cloud boundaries; we'll provide estimates in the pricing sheet.
[02:05] Amira: For the dedicated tier, what's the lead time to provision? We have an internal target to go live before the autumn promo window (early Sept).
[02:15] Maya: If we sign amendment end of June, provisioning EU dedicated pool with baseline capacity could be 4-6 weeks, shorter if we can accept a small initial baseline and stagger activation.
[02:28] Sofia: Procurement will push for a 12-month commitment instead of month-to-month; what are the discount bands?
[02:34] Maya: We propose a 12-month committed base with optional burst credits. Discount depends on committed tokens/month. I'll send the tiered pricing — large commits get ~18-25% savings vs on-demand.
[02:45] Amira: Okay, but we need the math for cost-per-1000 tokens with quantized models. We run a mix of chat and shorter completions.
[02:55] Carlos: We'll include cost curves for different seq lengths and the quantized performance profiles. Note: quantized models also slightly change latency; we'll flag tradeoffs.
[03:10] Jonas: On security — we require KMS integration and audit logs. Do you have HSM options?
[03:17] Carlos: We integrate customer KMS; for on-prem/Private deployments we support HSM-backed key management through your KMS provider. Audit logs and tracer events are available; we'll compile the specifics in the artifact pack.
[03:30] Amira: Also auditors asked about data retention and purge controls — can we keep logs in-region and purge after 90 days?
[03:38] Maya: Yes, log retention policies are configurable per account. We can commit to region-bound storage for audit logs for the EU pool.
[03:46] Sofia: Timeline: procurement wants legal redlines by 2028-06-25. Are you comfortable with that?
[03:53] Maya: We'll aim for that. It depends on the complexity of the amendment but we'll send proposed language by 2028-06-18.
[04:00] Amira: Great. Now, about burst — we need guaranteed burst up to 3x baseline for four windows per year, with a pre-warn of 48 hours. Is that part of the committed plan?
[04:10] Carlos: We can do a reserved base plus burst credits model. Burst pools are pre-warmed capacity; you can reserve guaranteed burst windows. There is a higher unit price for burst but it's cheaper than ad-hoc provision.
[04:22] Amira: What's the failover behavior if EU saturated during a flash sale? We can't have checkout degrade.
[04:30] Carlos: Two options: (1) keep traffic in EU and serve slightly slower (we can tune batching), (2) failover to a lower-cost US lighter model which may increase latency and cross-region data flow — both have tradeoffs. We'll recommend option 1 and designing backpressure on the app to gracefully queue.
[04:51] Jonas: How accurate are your traffic shaping and autoscale estimates? We want to avoid cold starts during peaks.
[04:56] Carlos: We have continuous batching plus AVX optimizations; autoscale can spin up within ~30-90s depending on instance pool. For very short spikes it's better to have reserved burst.
[05:10] Amira: OK. Could you run a 2-hour benchmark with our checkout traces to validate 95th pct? What's required from us?
[05:18] Carlos: We'll need sample trace payloads and a tokenization map; anonymized traces are fine. Jonas will help with peering details. We can schedule the bench in EU-west.
[05:29] Jonas: I can package 24 hours of representative traffic and extract a 2-hour peak window. Will that work?
[05:35] Carlos: Yes. Also include request distribution and typical seq lengths. We usually run bench at 1.0x and 3.0x baseline to emulate burst.
[05:44] Amira: Sounds good. We'll aim to deliver by 2028-06-20.
[05:48] Sofia: On contract items — we need a clause about service credits tied to 95th pct not being met on dedicated pool. Is that standard?
[05:56] Maya: We can include SLOs and an SLA credit table for dedicated customers; specifics depend on our support tier. We'll propose language.
[06:04] Amira: One more: we run sensitive PII in some flows; if we move routing to US accidentally that's a compliance risk. We need explicit no cross-border fallback unless we opt in.
[06:15] Maya: Absolutely. We'll add hard policy guardrails per account. Carlos: technically we can lock routing to region and disable cross-region fallback.
[06:26] Jonas: For VPC peering, what is the configuration model? Is it an IPsec tunnel or cloud peering?
[06:33] Carlos: For EU dedicated we offer both: cloud provider VPC peering in supported clouds or a managed IPsec VPN tunnel for on-prem. We'll include diagrams.
[06:41] Amira: Regarding on-prem, we might pilot a Private instance in Q4 for our most sensitive workloads. Is there an extra onboarding SLA?
[06:50] Maya: Private pilots have a longer lead time and a professional services package; we can outline options and a PS estimate.
[06:56] Sofia: Procurement question — can we get a one-time onboarding credit for migration?
[06:59] Maya: We can propose a small onboarding credit for a 12-month commit; I'll include an example in pricing.
[07:06] [crosstalk] Jonas: — if we do the pilot, network team will need runbooks..
[07:10] Carlos: We'll provide runbooks and a staging checklist.
[07:14] Amira: On the models side — your catalog lists quantized variants. Are those functionally identical?
[07:20] Carlos: Functionally similar but small delta in output quality for edge cases; we can run regression evals on your prompt set to show differences.
[07:29] Amira: Please do that — we can't accept regressions on customer-facing copy.
[07:34] Maya: We'll run evals as part of the bench and include a short quality report.
[07:40] Sofia: Back to timeline: procurement needs final numbers to present on 2028-06-26. Can you commit to getting pricing and legal draft by 2028-06-18?
[07:49] Maya: Yes, public commitment: pricing spreadsheet and amendment draft by 2028-06-18. Carlos will push SOC/ISO artifacts by 6/16.
[07:58] Amira: Good. Anything else?
[08:02] Jonas: A small concern — in past we've seen KV cache thrash when seq length varies a lot. Can you mitigate?
[08:10] Carlos: We're aware; our cache eviction policy can be tuned and we can pre-warm prefixes for checkout endpoints. We'll annotate the caching config in the runbook.
[08:22] Amira: Also want to mention we were evaluating VertigoAI's reserved throughput. Why choose Redwood? Cost and the runtime stability have been good, but we need better transparency on tail latency.
[08:35] Maya: Understood — we'll share latency profiles and a proposed mitigation plan.
[08:40] Sofia: Procurement flagged a clause around subprocessing — who else has access to raw requests inside Redwood?
[08:47] Carlos: Access is tightly controlled; only designated infra personnel, logs are masked by default, and we can add access audits into the agreement.
[08:56] Amira: One last operational ask — can we get token-level cost per route so product owners can see which features are driving spend?
[09:03] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns per route and model; we'll enable a dashboard for your team in staging.
[09:11] Jonas: Any blockers on our side? I need to confirm firewall egress rules with security team.
[09:16] Amira: We'll coordinate.
[09:18] Maya: Ok wrapping — to recap: Redwood will share pricing + amendment (Maya) by 2028-06-18; Carlos shares SOC/ISO and Private runbook by 2028-06-16; NorthGlen provides traffic samples by 2028-06-20; schedule bench for week of 6/25. Action owners captured.
[09:35] Sofia: Thanks, we'll look for the docs.
[09:38] Amira: Thanks everyone.
[09:40] Maya: Appreciate the time. We'll follow up in email with links and a meeting invite for the benchmark. Bye.
[09:46] [call ends]
notes: Customer emphasized strict no cross-border fallback; procurement deadlines are tight; technical bench is gating the SLA language. Some words auto-transcribed ("K V cash" for KV cache) and a few proper nouns may be off in the transcript.
